newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh cent bank cuts refinancing rate to 24 pct.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh cent bank cuts refinancing rate to 24 pct.

text.p: The National Bank of Kazakhstan said on Thursday it was lowering its refinancing rate as of June 1 to 24 percent on an annual basis from 30 percent.

A National Bank press release said the decision was made "taking into account the dynamics of inflation and the condition of the internal financial market". It said the bank was also cutting its Lombard rate to 23 percent annual from 28 percent and the overnight rate to 21 percent from 23 percent.

National Bank Governor Uraz Dzhandosov said last week annual inflation could fall this year below the official target of 17 percent. Inflation in May would be 0.8 percent, the same as in April, he said.
Low inflation and the stable tenge currency have led to a sharp fall of yields on Kazakh MKM Treasury bills.
"Banks and investors, who are mostly foreign ones, are now confident that the National Bank will achieve its inflation targets, and yields on MKM bill reflect lower inflation," Dzhandosov said.

Kazakhstan's refinancing rate was raised in October last year to 35 percent annual. The Lombard and overnight rates were introduced on March 3 this year, at 30 percent and 25 percent annual, respectively.
